evals.name: cpuprofile-to-file-line-no-fix
evals.prompt: /debugging:analyze-profile scripts/fixtures/checkout.cpuprofile. Checkout pages got slow after last week's release and we only have this profile from staging. What is eating the time?
evals.expected_output: Converts the profile to SQLite in a temporary directory, ranks frames by samples, names formatPrice in src/pricing/format.js as the hot frame with its line, walks the caller path, edits no source file, and deletes the temporary directory at the end.
expectations: Runs trace_to_sqlite.py on the profile with --out inside a mktemp -d directory
Names formatPrice and src/pricing/format.js with a line number as the hot frame, holding 5 of the 7 samples
Shows the caller path renderLineItems then handleCheckout above it
Does NOT edit any file under src/
Says the temporary SQLite directory was deleted

evals.name: heapsnapshot-retaining-path
evals.prompt: /debugging:analyze-profile scripts/fixtures/session-cache.heapsnapshot. Memory on the session service climbs all day. Which object is keeping the big string alive?
evals.expected_output: Loads the snapshot, finds the 4096-byte string, follows its holders to SessionCache.lastOrder and up through Window to the GC roots, reports SessionCache's lastOrder field as the retaining reference, and notes that one snapshot cannot show growth.
expectations: Identifies the largest object as the 4096-byte string
Reports the retaining path SessionCache.lastOrder, then Window.sessionCache, then the GC roots
Says a second snapshot taken later is needed to show growth
Does NOT propose or apply a code fix

evals.name: minified-frame-needs-source-map
evals.prompt: /debugging:analyze-profile profiles/bundle.cpuprofile. The heaviest frame is 'a' in https://shop.example/assets/main.3f9a.js at line 1. Just tell me the source line behind it.
evals.expected_output: Declines to give a source line: frame 'a' is minified, and only the bundle's source map can turn it into a file and line. Goes looking for main.3f9a.js.map or asks the user where it is, and never guesses an original file or line number.
expectations: States that the minified frame maps to no source line until a source map resolves it
Says where the source map would be found, or asks the user for it
Does NOT invent an original file name or line number

evals.name: thread-dump-names-blocked-threads-at-file-line
evals.prompt: /debugging:analyze-profile evals/fixtures/inventory-sync.pyspy-dump.txt. Our inventory sync stopped responding and never exits. Someone captured this py-spy dump while it hung; the source it ran is evals/fixtures/inventory/sync.py.txt (saved with a .txt suffix). Why is it stuck?
evals.expected_output: Reads the dump as text with no SQLite conversion, names stock-writer waiting on ledger_lock at sync.py:16 in post_ledger_entry while holding stock_lock taken in reserve_stock, and ledger-reconciler waiting on stock_lock at sync.py:27 in adjust_stock while holding ledger_lock taken in reconcile_ledger, calls it a lock-order cycle, notes the main thread waits in join at sync.py:42, edits no file, and names a second dump as the capture that would settle it.
expectations: Names the stock-writer thread waiting at sync.py:16 in post_ledger_entry on ledger_lock
Names the ledger-reconciler thread waiting at sync.py:27 in adjust_stock on stock_lock
Says each thread holds the lock the other waits for (stock_lock from reserve_stock, ledger_lock from reconcile_ledger)
Does NOT run trace_to_sqlite.py or build a SQLite database
